I will do chili again on my 2.2 mu, same as last year, because on a small piece like mine I do not want to gamble. I have farmed a long time, so I start from what worked before and what I see other people around me doing. Chili eats fertilizer, and if I cut too much I will lose yield, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the plants stay thin. I will use a hybrid seed because the ones people plant now set fruit more evenly and sell better than the old seed. For land prep I will plough first, then make ridges. I have well water, so I will not let the field go dry; I will water after transplanting, then again at flowering and fruit-setting, and a few more times if the weather stays dry. I will spray several times because chili is easy to get insects and leaf disease, and once it gets bad it is hard to pull back. On my small farm I count every yuan, so I will keep to one steady plan: enough base fertilizer, some topdressing, enough water, and regular spraying, not fancy things.
